canvas.note: Matches the native size of the real reference posters exactly, so proportions transfer directly instead of being re-derived at a different scale.

_why_this_exists: Two separate jobs. (1) VOCABULARY: a closed set of values the LLM picks from when writing a design brief -- it never invents a value, so every possible brief maps to something actually implemented. (2) TOKENS: fixed spacing/type scales, so nothing is an arbitrary hand-picked number. Earlier versions failed on both: the LLM had no say in visual direction, and CSS values were ad-hoc (8,10,14,16,18,20,22,24,26 scattered across rules), which is a large part of why output read as generic.

spacing._note: Everything on the poster uses ONE of these. No in-between values.

type_scale._note: Deliberately DRAMATIC ratios (title is 4-6x body, not 2x) -- the values render.js actually uses per layout_family are now hardcoded per family to match their specific reference poster, but stay within this same scale.

radius._note: Small. References are mostly flat/sharp; heavy rounding reads as dated.

shadow._note: Used sparingly and only where a real element floats above another. Earlier versions added shadows to compensate for flat layouts -- that is the wrong instinct.

composition_rules._note: v13 tried to teach these as AI-followed RULES (leave a third empty, anchor to one edge...) and the model didn't reliably apply them -- output still read as generic. v14 bakes them into the fixed geometry of each layout_family instead (see render.js): the model can no longer under- or over-apply restraint because it no longer controls spacing at all, only content. This block is now documentation of what's baked in, not an instruction the model reads.

vocabulary._note: The LLM picks ONE value per field. Anything outside these lists is rejected and falls back to a safe default. layout_family is the only field that affects LAYOUT -- once picked, every position/size/decoration for that family is fixed in render.js, measured directly off the specific reference poster(s) named below. The model supplies content (text/photo/palette) into that fixed template; it does not author spacing, sizing, or ornament choices any more (that discretion is what made v13's output read as generic 'a design' instead of this organisation's actual design).

layout_family._note: Picked BEFORE anything else -- the single biggest lever on whether a poster looks like this organisation's work. Each entry names the exact reference(s) it was measured from; open backend/references/<file> to see the source.
layout_family.photo_band: Full-bleed photo on the top 76% of the canvas, a solid colour band (palette base) on the bottom 24%, title straddling the seam. Default choice for a single product/subject with a short supporting paragraph -- produce, a place, an object, a short announcement. Measured from ref_01.jpg.
layout_family.full_bleed_photo: Photo fills the whole canvas, text in the photo's quiet zone carried by type weight, no band, no card. Reserve for strong atmospheric/scenic photography where the photo itself is the whole statement. Measured from ref_03.jpg / ref_06.jpg.
layout_family.stat_grid: Headline, then a 2-4 tile grid -- each tile a cream caption bar (big number + label) directly above its own photo. Use only when the content genuinely has 2-4 countable achievements/facts. Measured from ref_08.jpg.
layout_family.photo_feature_list: Two-line headline, then 2-4 rows of [photo thumbnail + bold heading + one-line description]. Use when the content is a set of distinct points, not one idea. Measured from ref_12.jpg.
layout_family.portrait_quote: Portrait photo across the top ~46%, fading into the palette base colour, a large pull-quote below. Use ONLY for an attributed statement from a named person -- never invent a quote for content that isn't actually one. Measured from ref_09.jpg.

occasion.none: No specific occasion -- general announcement or campaign.
occasion.national_day: Saudi National Day (Sept 23). Green-forward, national identity.
occasion.founding_day: Founding Day (Feb 22). Heritage/earth tones, historic character.
occasion.saudi_identity: General Saudi identity framing without a specific date.
occasion.harvest_season: Agricultural season, harvest, produce (e.g. a dates season).

mood._note: Informs palette choice and copy tone only -- it no longer touches layout (that's fixed per layout_family now).
mood.reverent: Quiet, spacious, deep tones, minimal ornament.
mood.energetic: Bold type, strong contrast, tighter crops.
mood.calm: Soft gradients, light palette, generous space.

palettes._note: Hand-built, each capped at base + 2 accents, all derived from colors measured in the real reference posters rather than invented.

defaults._note: Used when the LLM is unavailable, or when it returns a value outside the vocabulary.
